title: (Obj) for the constructible cocone
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $X$ a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian. The
constructible cocone ([def-sfb-constructible-cocone]) satisfies (Obj) of
[sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit]: every $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to
$T_{E,\Qlb}K_E$ for some finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$ and some
$K_E\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$.

proof.text: Fix the coefficient conventions before invoking descent. The ring $\underline E$ has sections $C(S,E)$ by [def-sfb-padic-subfield-condensed-ring], and $\underline{\Qlb}(S)$ consists of the continuous functions valued in a finite subextension by [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Both are pulled back using the same $p_X^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], and by [def-sfb-dcons-subfield] and [def-sfb-dcons-qlbar] the cocone categories $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ and $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$ are the bounded constructible categories of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] over exactly these pulled-back rings $E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ and $\QbarX=p_X^*\underline{\Qlb}$. Thus the coefficient rings denoted $E_X^c,\Omega_X^c$ in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category] are exactly $E_X,\QbarX$ here. In [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], finite presentation means a cokernel of a map between finite sums of the regular module. Consequently [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented] and [def-sfb-constructible-module] give exactly the stratified local cokernel presentations used in that condensed module category. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], the resulting bounded categories are the same full subcategories of the same ambient derived module categories. This identification imposes no completeness condition and does not replace local finite presentation by the stronger scalar-constant-model convention.

source.place: Modules and Complexes paragraphs; unit proof (3), finite sheaf descent followed by Postnikov induction

proof.text: For a finite field $E$ put $\mathcal C_E=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$, and let $\mathcal D=D(\Mod_{\QbarX})$. Since $X$ is topologically Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-finite-model-proof-api] makes $\mathcal C_E$ triangulated. By [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus], extension to a finite field or to $\Qlb$ is exact on modules, its derived functor is termwise tensor, and it preserves shifts and distinguished triangles. These are the specified functors $T_{E,F}$ and $T_{E,\Qlb}$ by [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], using step 1. Use the cocone [def-sfb-constructible-cocone], now with its vertex included in $\mathcal D$: its transition functors, scalar-extension functors and comparisons supply a cocone with triangulated source categories and triangulated functors $\Phi_E:\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal D$. The target inclusion preserves triangles because its triangles are the inherited ambient ones.

source.place: Modules and Complexes paragraphs; unit proof (3), finite sheaf descent followed by Postnikov induction

proof.text: Let $P(Y)$ mean that $Y\in\mathcal D$ is isomorphic to $\Phi_E(K_E)$ for some finite $E$ and $K_E\in\mathcal C_E$. The index is nonempty and directed by [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Any ambient morphism $\Phi_E(K_E)\to\Phi_F(L_F)$ is a morphism in the full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$; [lem-sfb-constructible-cocone-hom-surj] therefore descends it to one common finite stage, with precisely the cocone comparisons. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-directed-triangulated-image] now hold for the ambient cocone of step 2. It follows that $P$ is triangulated: it contains zero, is stable under shifts, and is closed under extensions in distinguished triangles. It is also invariant under isomorphism: compose the isomorphism exhibiting a model with the given isomorphism of target objects. This is the cone-lifting mechanism required by the unit's Postnikov argument; it makes no claim that a single stage functor is full.

source.place: Modules and Complexes paragraphs; unit proof (3), finite sheaf descent followed by Postnikov induction

proof.text: Every constructible $\QbarX$-module $M$ has a model for its degree-zero complex. Indeed its finite stratification and local finite presentations are exactly those checked in step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-finite-presentation-descent] gives a finite $E$, a constructible $E_X$-module $M_E$, and an isomorphism $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}M_E\cong M$. The complex $M_E[0]$ lies in $\mathcal C_E$ by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]: its only possible nonzero cohomology is $M_E$, and zero modules have the presentation $E_X^0\to E_X^0\to0$. Exact, termwise scalar extension from [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus] identifies $\Phi_E(M_E[0])$ with $M[0]$. Thus $P(M[0])$, and step 3 gives $P(M[0][-q])$ for every integer $q$. The cited sheaf-descent theorem supplies the gluing across strata as well as the local coefficient models; a local matrix argument alone would not give this conclusion.

source.place: Modules and Complexes paragraphs; unit proof (3), finite sheaf descent followed by Postnikov induction

proof.text:
Take $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$ and choose integers $a\le b$ with $H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, as in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Represent $K$ by a complex and use its standard truncations. For every $q$ the triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] is
$$\tau_{\le q-1}K\longrightarrow\tau_{\le q}K\longrightarrow H^q(K)[-q]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\le q-1}K)[1].$$
Induct for $q=a,\ldots,b$ on $P(\tau_{\le q}K)$. The initial truncation $\tau_{\le a-1}K$ is acyclic and hence isomorphic to zero in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so it has $P$ by step 3. At the induction step, $H^q(K)$ is constructible by the chosen category definition, so its shifted single complex has $P$ by step 4. Extension closure of $P$ from step 3 gives $P(\tau_{\le q}K)$. Finally $\tau_{\le b}K\to K$ is a quasi-isomorphism, since it induces the identity on the surviving cohomology and both sides have zero cohomology above $b$. Hence $P(K)$. This is a finite induction, including the acyclic case, and therefore ends with one finite coefficient field.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; applied to the unit proof (3), Complexes paragraph

proof.text: Unpack $P(K)$ to obtain $E$ and $K_E\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ with $T_{E,\Qlb}K_E\cong K$ in the ambient derived category. Both objects belong to the full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$, so this is also an isomorphism in that subcategory. The cocone [def-sfb-constructible-cocone] has these very scalar-extension functors; this proves exactly (Obj) of [sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit].
